featured_reviews.name: Dubey Chandan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Utsav Cuisine, Powai – Simple, Satisfying, and Safe Choice

So I tried Utsav Cuisine in Powai and honestly, it’s one of those places that doesn’t scream for attention but quietly delivers a decent meal. Not too fancy, not too dramatic just simple Indian food done right.

The ambience is basic but clean. No flashy lights or trendy decor, just a calm and decent dining space where you can sit peacefully and eat without loud music or selfie-crazy crowds. It’s more of a family place than a hangout spot.

We ordered a few North Indian dishes – butter naan, paneer butter masala, dal tadka and jeera rice. The taste was good, nothing out-of-this-world, but definitely satisfying. The paneer was soft and the gravy was creamy. Dal had that homemade touch and the rice was well-cooked. So overall, you won’t be disappointed, but you also won’t be jumping out of your seat with excitement.

Service was fine. Not too fast, not too slow. Staff was polite, answered our questions, and didn’t hover too much.

Prices are reasonable for the quantity and quality. You get good value for a peaceful meal without burning your wallet.

So yeah, Utsav is not a place you’d choose for a celebration or a date night, but it’s definitely a safe pick for a casual lunch or dinner when you just want a good Indian meal without any drama. Average overall, but in a good way.

featured_reviews.name: Sakshi Tiwari
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this restaurant yesterday as a group, and initially, the experience was quite good. The food was really delicious, and the ambiance had a calm and relaxing vibe, which we genuinely appreciated. We also noticed the “Atithi Devo Bhava” quote and admired the values it represents.

However, the experience took a disappointing turn toward the end.

We had spent less than an hour in the restaurant when we were asked to pay the bill quickly because billing was about to close. Immediately after making the payment, one of the staff members told us to leave, even though one of our group members was still eating.

This felt very disrespectful and rushed. Another server, who had been attending us from the beginning and was quite friendly while talking about their other branches like Mantra and Laxmi Pure Veg, just stood there smiling while this happened, which made it even more awkward.

The staff member even said, “Bar jaisa nahi hai ki late tak chalu rahega,” which was unnecessary and inappropriate. We were not there for drinks, and it is basic understanding that customers usually take at least 1 to 1.5 hours to finish their meals comfortably.

If the restaurant cannot accommodate customers for a reasonable dining duration, they should inform guests beforehand or stop accepting new customers at that time.

Being asked to leave immediately after paying, especially on our first visit, was extremely disappointing and left a bad impression.

If you truly believe in “Atithi Devo Bhava,” then please reflect that in how you treat your customers.

featured_reviews.name: Ashu Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Serious Food Safety Concern at Utsav Restaurant
My partner and I visited Utsav today and ordered chicken tikka and paneer tikka. Within just 10 minutes of eating the chicken tikka at the restaurant, I began experiencing severe stomach pain and was unable to finish my meal. For the next 4 hours, I suffered greatly, ultimately vomiting everything out.
The situation worsened when my partner, who had taken her order home, also fell severely ill around 2:30 AM and began vomiting as well.
We spent the entire night unwell and are still not feeling better.
I sincerely urge the Maharashtra Government Food Quality Inspectors to investigate this restaurant, particularly the quality and hygiene standards of their chicken and paneer tikka. No customer should have to go through this experience after dining out.

featured_reviews.name: Chaitanya Jagtap
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience.

We visited Utsav Restaurant in Powai expecting to avail a 10–20% cashback offer through Zomato, which was one of the main reasons we chose this place. However, when it was time to pay, the staff outright refused to accept payment via Zomato without giving any proper explanation. This felt misleading and unprofessional.

To make matters worse, from entry to finishing most of our dinner, including wait time, we only spent around 50 minutes in total. Despite this, the staff rushed us to complete the payment, saying their billing was about to close even though one of us was still eating. Right after we paid, they asked us to leave while our meal wasn’t even fully finished.

This kind of behavior is unacceptable and completely ruined the dining experience. Poor service, lack of transparency, and no regard for customer comfort. Definitely not recommended.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for your feedback, Chaitanya.
We’d like to clarify that Utsav Cuisine is not a partner under Zomato Dining, and therefore cashbacks or bill payments via Zomato are not applicable at our restaurant. We operate only on a standard listing for visibility. Expecting platform-specific offers without confirming participation may lead to misunderstandings such as this.
Regarding your comments on service, our team did inform about billing closure timelines. However, we agree that this should have been communicated more politely and without making guests feel rushed. We will address this internally.
We stand by our commitment to provide a good dining experience and regret that this visit did not meet your expectations.
We truly value every guest who chooses to dine with us, and your feedback helps us improve both communication and service. We hope you will consider visiting us again for a better experience.
Warm Regards,
Team Utsav Cuisine.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The experience was honestly just average. Starting with the positives — the ambience is great and the views are beautiful. You get a lovely view of Powai Lake and the city skyline on one side, and lush green hills on the other, which makes the place feel really nice and relaxing. The service was good overall, and valet parking is available, which is definitely convenient.

That said, the rest of the experience was quite disappointing. The tables, plates, and cutlery were not properly clean, which was a major letdown for a place at this price point. Even the regular drinking water jar had visible dust and stains on it, which was quite off-putting. The food was mostly average. We had ordered the khow suey — the taste was good, but everything was already mixed together when served, which was disappointing as it takes away from the whole experience of customizing it with the toppings yourself. The rest of the dishes were just okay, with nothing particularly memorable or worth talking about. The music was also quite bad and took away from the overall vibe instead of adding to it.

Considering the pricing, the experience simply doesn’t justify the cost. You’re largely paying for the view, but beyond that, it felt overpriced for what was offered.

featured_reviews.name: Prithu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yuhi is honestly one of the better hidden gems in Powai if you are looking for a lively night out with good food, great drinks, and proper atmosphere.

The place is spacious enough to comfortably handle large groups without feeling cramped, which already earns it points in Mumbai. The ambience really comes alive at night, especially with the laser projections lighting up the mountainside and the DJ setup sitting dramatically on its own balcony like it is preparing for a Tomorrowland set.

The drinks here are genuinely excellent, and the food absolutely keeps up. The butter chicken and biryani are must tries, rich, flavorful, and actually memorable instead of just “good enough for a lounge.” The starters are solid too and pair really well with the drinks.

Another underrated touch is the mist cooling system, which makes a huge difference during warmer evenings. That said, the place definitely shines more during nighttime or cooler weather when the open air vibe fully works in its favor.

Final verdict: Great ambience, excellent drinks, genuinely good food, and enough personality to stand out in Powai’s crowded dining scene. The kind of place you go to once and immediately start planning a second visit.

The Cold Brew Iced Tea was refreshing with a strong brewed tea flavor, a hint of lemon, and very mild sweetness.

The Virgin Grapefruit Cobbler stood out with its bold, fresh pomegranate flavor.

For starters,
the Mushroom Krapow (Vegetable Oyster Basil) was delicious. Slightly sweet, full of flavor, and perfect for mushroom lovers.

The Thai Style Momo was a highlight for me. Soft vegetable momos dunked in a red Thai curry-style sauce. Absolutely loved this one.

The Mushroom Roast Pizza was honestly one of the best pizzas I’ve ever had—perfectly roasted, loaded with mushrooms, cheese, walnuts, arugula, and a drizzle of balsamic. Absolutely loved it.

The Spaghetti Aglio Olio was simple yet amazing—garlic, chilli, olive oil, parsley, and aged parmesan done just right.

Overall, great vibes, amazing food, and refreshing drinks. I’ll definitely be visiting again ✨

featured_reviews.review_text:
Gurukripa Bar on Saki Vihar Road, Powai is one of those classic neighbourhood bars that has built a strong reputation purely on the strength of its food. I recently visited with friends and overall had a very satisfying experience, making it a solid 4-star destination for anyone in and around Powai looking for good food and a lively evening.

Let me start with the food, which is undoubtedly the highlight here. We ordered several starters along with a basic main course, and every dish was well-prepared and full of flavour. The absolute star of the meal was the mutton — incredibly tender, perfectly cooked, and rich in taste. If you are a mutton lover, this place will not disappoint you. In fact, the Dehati Mutton is a must-try. It is slow-cooked beautifully, packed with traditional flavours, and has that authentic rustic taste that is hard to find these days. Easily one of the best mutton dishes you can have in this area.

The starters were fresh and satisfying, and the gravies paired very well with rotis and rice. Portion sizes are generous, making it a good value-for-money place when dining with friends or in a group.

Another thing that truly impressed me was the speed of service. Even when the bar is packed, the staff manages to serve food in a decent amount of time. This shows excellent coordination between the kitchen and the service team, which is not easy to maintain during peak hours. Despite the crowd, our orders arrived quickly and were served hot, which added to the overall positive experience.

That said, timing your visit is extremely important. I would strongly recommend avoiding Friday nights unless you enjoy a loud, high-energy crowd. The place gets extremely crowded with corporate groups, and after 7 PM, finding a table becomes next to impossible. It also gets very noisy, which personally is not my preference when I want to relax and have a peaceful conversation with friends. I prefer quieter places, and Friday nights here can feel overwhelming.

If you still plan to visit on a busy day, the best time to reach is between 6:30 PM and 7 PM. After that, the crowd increases rapidly.

The ambience is typical of a popular local bar — lively, energetic, and social. It’s not a luxury lounge, but it has its own charm for people who enjoy a bustling atmosphere.

I am also cutting one star and giving 4 stars instead of 5 because of the pan shop owner outside the bar. I strongly believe these pan shops are indirectly part of the bar experience, and it is every bar’s responsibility to ensure that the outside environment is managed well. The first impression matters, and it should reflect the quality inside.

Overall, Gurukripa Bar delivers where it matters most — excellent food, especially mutton, fast service, and good value for money. With smart timing and the right expectations, it’s a fantastic place for a satisfying evening out.

If you go, don’t miss the Dehati Mutton — it’s an absolute must-try.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Chili’s Grill & Bar in Powai, and overall, it was a solid 4-star experience. Chili’s has always been known for its dependable food quality, and that part still remains intact. We ordered the Chicken Platter, which comes with a nice customisation option. The portion size was good, the flavours were balanced, and everything was served hot and well-prepared. It’s the kind of comfort food Chili’s is known for, and it didn’t disappoint.

For drinks, I tried their Mango Mocktail, and it was easily one of the highlights of the evening. Refreshing, smooth, and perfectly sweet — I liked it so much that I ended up ordering it twice. Their beer selection was also good, maintaining the familiar Chili’s standard.

However, a few things held the experience back from being a full 5-star visit. The first noticeable issue was the pre-added 10% tip on the bill. While I fully support tipping for good service, adding it automatically and at a relatively high percentage didn’t feel right — especially considering the level of service we received. The service wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t exceptional enough to justify a mandatory 10% charge. Tips should always feel voluntary and earned, not forced.

The ambience also felt different compared to the older Chili’s outlets. One thing that always made Chili’s special was its distinct American pub-style vibe — warm lighting, rustic interiors, and a lively but cozy atmosphere. The Powai outlet, unfortunately, doesn’t quite capture that same charm. The décor and layout feel more like a typical modern Indian pub, lacking the signature Chili’s personality that many of us associate with the brand. It’s decent, but it doesn’t stand out the way earlier Chili’s interiors used to.

That said, the environment is still comfortable for dining, and the place is clean, spacious, and well-maintained. The overall quality of food and drinks remains trustworthy, and if you’re looking for a casual evening out with good food, Chili’s Powai is still a reliable choice.

In summary, the experience was enjoyable — great food, excellent mocktails, and a relaxed vibe — but with room for improvement in service transparency and ambience. A good outing overall, deserving of four stars.

We went to Mainland China on Monday to try some nice authentic Chinese food. Surprisingly, they had a Six Course Set Menu starting at ₹795 for veg and ₹895 for non-veg and honestly, it’s worth every penny.

We both tried the veg and non-veg options and loved everything from start to finish. The food was absolutely delicious and tasted genuinely authentic. Even the Cantonese Clear Soup, at first, looks like just plain water, but once you taste it, you won’t stop. The flavor is so comforting and light, yet rich in taste.

For dumplings, we had Truffle Oil Infused Edamame, Corn and Water Chestnut, Sriracha Chicken, and Chicken Siu Mai. All were perfectly steamed and flavorful.

In starters, we tried Turnip Cake Salt and Pepper, Jiang’s Chilli Cottage Cheese, Chicken with Assorted Pepper, and Sliced Chicken in Chilli Oil with Spring Onion. Every dish was cooked to perfection.

For the main course, we went with Stir Fried Chinese Greens, Vegetables in Yellow Bean Sauce, Fish in Roasted Garlic Sauce, and Stir Fried Chicken in Mountain Chilli Sauce. These were paired beautifully with Korean Sweet Potato Noodles, Wok Tossed Hakka Noodles, and Edamame Jasmine Fried Rice.

The dessert, Honey Noodles with Almond Flakes served with a Chocolate Cigar Roll, was the highlight of the meal. It’s crunchy, chocolaty, and so addictive that you’ll want another serving.

We also tried their mocktails, which were quite refreshing and paired well with the food.

Overall, the experience was amazing from the service to the presentation. At this price, the Six Course Lunch Menu is totally worth it. It’s available only on weekdays during lunch, so plan accordingly.

Definitely recommended if you’re looking for a satisfying and authentic Chinese meal without spending too much.

The menu’s filled.

⭐ Highly Recommended for Authentic Maharashtrian & Seafood Lovers! ⭐

Hotel Malvan Katta, located at Vikhroli West on LBS Marg, just opposite HCC, is a must-visit place for anyone who enjoys authentic Maharashtrian and Indian seafood.

We tried a variety of fish thalis, and the taste and quality were excellent and truly commendable. The food felt fresh, flavorful, and homely. The prices are very reasonable, especially for thalis, biryani, and other menu items.

The quantity is impressive—we tried prawns biryani, boneless chicken biryani, and also explored the veg menu. Dishes like veg biryani, veg pulao, and paneer biryani were absolutely delicious and served in generous portions.

Overall, it’s a decent place to try some authentic Malvani flavours.

The service was prompt and friendly. The staff was attentive and helped us with recommendations from their speciality dishes, which made the experience even better.

featured_reviews.name: anurag kasbe
featured_reviews.review_text:
China Valley Restaurant Review

Recently, I had the chance to visit China Valley, a spot that combines a good ambience with the convenience of valet parking. The experience was overall enjoyable, though there were a few hiccups along the way.

Ambience and Service:
The ambience at China Valley is inviting, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal. The service, however, was just okay. The staff was polite, but there was a bit of a mix-up when they brought out the appetizer and soup together, which felt a little rushed.

The Food:

•	Chicken Manchow Soup: This was the first dish I tried, and it did not disappoint. The soup was flavorful and just the right level of spicy—perfect for kicking off the meal.
•	Mongolian Pan Fried Chicken: Next, I went for the Mongolian Pan Fried Chicken. While it was decent, it could have been much better with a touch more seasoning. It felt like it was almost there but just missed the mark slightly.
•	Chicken Pot Rice: For the main course, I had the Chicken Pot Rice, which turned out to be the highlight of the meal. The rice was well-cooked, the chicken was tender, and the quantity was generous, making it a satisfying dish overall.

Drinks:
I ordered a glass of tonic water, which was refreshing, while my partner enjoyed a glass of red wine. The drinks were well-served and complemented the meal nicely.

Final Thoughts:
China Valley offers good food in a pleasant setting, though there is room for improvement in the service department. If you’re looking for a place with solid Chinese cuisine and a comfortable atmosphere, it’s worth a visit—just don’t be surprised if your soup and appetizer arrive at the same time!

Place looks clean (out common area is not so clean and soon as you sit agents of the food stalls descend on you offering their menu.
